parts.markdown:
Use our free **Utah paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Utah income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to understand how much money you could receive on payday.

Utah updated its payroll withholding schedules during 2026, reducing its withholding rate and adjusting the allowances used in employer calculations.

Whether you work in Salt Lake City, Provo, Ogden, St. George or another Utah community, understanding your net income can help you compare job offers and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the Utah Paycheck Calculator

Begin by selecting annual salary or hourly wages.

Enter your gross earnings before taxes and deductions.

Select your payment frequency. Enter federal and Utah income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include healthcare premiums, retirement contributions and other employee deductions. Use the full withholding amounts, including any extra tax withheld.

If your earnings are approaching annual payroll contribution limits, provide your year-to-date taxable wages.

Review your estimated gross pay, individual deductions and remaining take-home income.

Use your latest payroll statement to confirm the applicable taxable wage amounts.

## Utah Payroll Taxes in 2026

Visit the [Utah State Tax Commission](https://tax.utah.gov/) for official information about individual income tax and employer withholding.

## What Changed in Utah Income Tax in 2026?

Utah reduced its withholding rate from 4.50% to 4.45% for payroll periods beginning on or after June 1, 2026.

The revised withholding schedules also increased the base allowance and adjusted the income thresholds used to determine allowance reductions.

These changes mean a Utah employee may receive a different paycheck during the second half of 2026 even if their gross salary and employee benefits remain unchanged.

A reliable Utah salary calculator must account for the applicable payroll period rather than applying one configuration to the entire calendar year.

Review the official [Utah Publication 14 withholding guide](https://tax.utah.gov/forms-pubs/pub-14/) for the revised calculation schedules.

## How Utah Income Tax Withholding Works

Utah's ordinary employer withholding method starts with the applicable taxable wages multiplied by the withholding rate.

The employer then calculates an allowance adjustment that reduces the initial withholding amount.

This allowance gradually decreases as taxable wages rise.

Once the applicable allowance is completely phased out, ordinary withholding equals the taxable wage amount multiplied by 4.45%, subject to the applicable calculation and rounding method.

This differs from simply subtracting a fixed standard deduction from gross salary.

The [Utah employer withholding guidance](https://tax.utah.gov/business/withholding-overview/employers/) explains the information employers use when determining the appropriate deduction.

## Utah Withholding Allowances in 2026

The revised schedules use different allowance amounts and reduction thresholds according to filing classification and payment frequency.
The allowance is reduced by 1.3% of taxable wages exceeding the applicable threshold.

These are payroll calculation parameters rather than cash deductions or ordinary annual income tax return exemptions.

## How to Calculate Utah Income Tax Withholding

Consider a single employee receiving $400 in weekly Utah taxable wages under the revised June 2026 schedules.

Initial withholding:

$400 × 4.45% = $17.80.

Applicable base allowance: $9.

Wages exceeding the allowance reduction threshold:

$400 − $180 = $220.

Allowance reduction:

$220 × 1.3% = $2.86.

Remaining allowance:

$9 − $2.86 = $6.14.

The unrounded calculation produces $11.66 in withholding.

The official Utah Publication 14 worked example displays whole-dollar amounts and produces final withholding of $12.

Different authorized withholding methods may produce slightly different results because of rounding.

## Understanding Federal Form W-4 in Utah

Utah generally uses the employee's federal Form W-4 filing information to determine the appropriate state withholding classification.

Employees filing as head of household generally use the single Utah withholding schedule.

Federal credits, deductions and other withholding adjustments should not automatically be transferred into the Utah calculation.

Visit the [IRS Form W-4 resources](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-4) for federal certificate information and the Utah withholding guide for state-specific treatment.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Utah Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on taxable earnings, filing status, payment frequency and applicable Form W-4 information.

Employers use the official calculation methods in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered wages up to the annual taxable wage ceiling of $184,500 in 2026.

Ordinary Medicare applies at 1.45% of covered earnings without a standard annual wage ceiling.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% on Medicare-covered wages exceeding $200,000 paid by that employer during the calendar year.

Consult the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) and [Social Security Administration contribution limits](https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html) for more information.

## Utah Paycheck Example: $65,000 Salary

Consider an employee earning $65,000 annually and receiving 26 biweekly payments.

This example assumes ordinary single federal withholding settings, no additional benefit deductions, no annual payroll contribution limits reached and application of Utah's revised June 2026 withholding schedule using whole-dollar calculations.

At this earnings level, the ordinary single Utah withholding allowance has been fully reduced.

Your actual paycheck may differ depending on employer withholding methods and benefit arrangements.

## Utah Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Suppose you earn $28 per hour and work 40 regular hours plus five qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$28 × 40 = $1,120.

Overtime earnings:

$28 × 1.5 × 5 = $210.

Total gross earnings: $1,330.

Federal and Utah withholding and ordinary payroll contributions are then calculated using the applicable taxable wage amounts.

Review the [Utah Labor Commission](https://laborcommission.utah.gov/) and [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for applicable employment requirements.

## Working Across Utah State Borders

Employees working across Utah, Nevada, Idaho, Colorado or other neighboring states may have different withholding obligations depending on residency and employment location.

Utah also provides specific withholding exclusions for certain qualifying short-term nonresident employees.

These exclusions have eligibility requirements and should not automatically be applied to every temporary worker.

Consult the [Utah withholding guide](https://tax.utah.gov/forms-pubs/pub-14/) before claiming an interstate withholding exemption.

## Planning Your Utah Monthly Budget

Use estimated net income rather than gross annual salary when establishing spending limits.

Account for housing, transportation, healthcare, insurance, groceries and required debt payments.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a suitable savings target, while our [mortgage payment calculator](/calculators/mortgage-calculator/) can help estimate housing expenses.

The [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau financial education resources](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/) provide additional guidance for managing household finances.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Utah's income tax withholding rate in 2026?

The revised employer withholding rate is 4.45% for payroll periods beginning on or after June 1, 2026. Earlier payroll periods generally use the previous configuration.

### Does Salt Lake City have a separate personal income tax?

Salt Lake City generally does not impose a separate municipal personal wage income tax. Applicable federal and Utah payroll taxes still reduce earnings.

### Why is Utah withholding sometimes lower than 4.45% of my wages?

Utah's employer withholding calculation includes an allowance that can reduce the initial withholding amount. The allowance gradually decreases as taxable wages increase.

The results are educational estimates rather than official payroll calculations or individualized tax advice.
